01 · Building an LLM Application

§ Models and Prompts

Large Language ModelsAn LLM predicts tokens conditioned on the context

Several providers offer general-purpose models behind an API

Model SelectionChoose a model against application requirements

The cheapest model that clears our quality line

Autoregressive GenerationThe next token depends on the tokens already in context

Each chosen token becomes context for the next

Caveat: Plausible AnswersA fluent answer can be unsupported by the supplied facts

A specific answer with no evidence behind it

LLM Application Control FlowAn application adds processing before and after a model call

The LLM call is one stage inside a larger workflow

Application ComponentsModel interfaces connect prompts, data, and output handling

An application connects these components around the model call

LangChain Model InterfaceChoose a recorded response or a real locally served model

import { ChatOllama } from '@langchain/ollama';
import { FakeListChatModel } from '@langchain/core/utils/testing';

// Offline execution tests the application around a fixed response.
const replay = new FakeListChatModel({responses: [
  '{"label":"vibration","evidence":"vibrates"}'
]});
// Live inference requires an installed model and a running Ollama server.
const live = new ChatOllama({model: '<installed-chat-model>',
  baseUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:11434', temperature: 0});
// makeModel(responses) selects replay or live in the code windows.

Chat MessagesMessage roles distinguish instructions, user requests, and tool results

Roles separate policy, request, model output and tool result

Prompt TemplatesCompose reusable steps with LangChain.js core

const prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.fromMessages([
  ["system", "Classify notes as {labels}. Quote evidence."],
  ["human", "{note}"]
]);
const input = {labels: "leak, vibration, other",
  note: "Pump vibrates above 2500 rpm"};
const rendered = await prompt.invoke(input);
return rendered.toChatMessages().map(m => ({
  role: m.getType(), content: m.content
}));

§ Structured Outputs

Structured OutputA schema defines the shape of the response consumed by software

A schema turns the answer into data software can use

Output ValidationSyntax, schema, and meaning require different checks

Each check stops a different failure

Output Parsing and ValidationCompose reusable steps with LangChain.js core

const schema = z.object({
  label: z.enum(["leak", "vibration", "other"]),
  evidence: z.string().min(1)
}).strict();
const parser = new JsonOutputParser();
const note = "Pump vibrates above 2500 rpm";
const raw = '{"label":"vibration","evidence":"vibrates"}';
const parsed = await parser.invoke(raw);
const result = schema.parse(parsed);
if (!note.includes(result.evidence)) {
  throw new Error("Evidence is absent from the source");
}
return result;

02 · Connecting LLM Calls

§ Context and Memory

Conversation ContextA model call sees the messages supplied to that call

The application supplies the conversation history

Memory MechanismsKeep context selection separate from durable storage

Each mechanism sends a different part of the history

Conversation MemoryCompose reusable steps with LangChain.js core

const history = [
  new HumanMessage("Use Celsius. Monitor P-17."),
  new AIMessage("Which period?"),
  new HumanMessage("Last 24 hours."),
  new AIMessage("Which measurement?")
];
const keep = 2;
const recent = keep === 0 ? [] : history.slice(-keep);
const prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.fromMessages([
  ["system", "Report maintenance measurements."],
  new MessagesPlaceholder("history"), ["human", "{question}"]
]);
const value = await prompt.invoke({history: recent,
  question: "What was the maximum temperature?"});
return value.toChatMessages().map(m => m.content);

Window MemoryA bounded window can discard a fact that remains relevant

The window dropped the instruction from turn 1

Summary MemoryA summary trades token count for information loss

The summary lost the condition

Context BudgetInstructions, evidence, history, and output share a finite budget

Reserve the output before filling the context

Caveat: Untrusted ContextRetrieved text can include instructions that conflict with the task

Instructions inside retrieved text get no permissions

§ Chains and Routing

Sequential ChainThe output of one step becomes the input to the next

Step outputs form explicit dependencies

Parallel and Sequential StepsIndependent steps can run before their outputs are combined

Only dependencies require sequential execution

Sequential and Parallel ChainsCompose reusable steps with LangChain.js core

const prepare = RunnableLambda.from(note => note.trim());
const features = RunnableMap.from({
  equipment: RunnableLambda.from(s => s.match(/P-\d+/)?.[0] ?? null),
  characters: RunnableLambda.from(s => s.length)
});
const report = RunnableLambda.from(fields => ({
  ...fields, needsReview: fields.equipment === null
}));
const chain = prepare.pipe(features).pipe(report);
return await chain.invoke("  P-17 vibrates  ");

Router ChainA router selects a destination for the request

Routing chooses among defined destinations

Routing and FallbacksCompose reusable steps with LangChain.js core

const branches = {
  maintenance: RunnableLambda.from(x => ({queue: "maintenance", note: x.note})),
  production: RunnableLambda.from(x => ({queue: "production", note: x.note})),
  unknown: RunnableLambda.from(x => ({queue: "review", note: x.note}))
};
const router = RunnableLambda.from(async x => {
  const route = Object.hasOwn(branches, x.route) ? x.route : "unknown";
  return await branches[route].invoke(x);
});
return await router.invoke({route: "maintenance", note: "P-17 vibrates"});

Caveat: Error PropagationA downstream step can hide an upstream extraction error

An early extraction error makes the whole report wrong

Complete LLM ApplicationRender messages, invoke a model, parse JSON, and validate evidence

const prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.fromMessages([
  ["system", 'Return JSON with label and evidence. Use leak, vibration, or other.'],
  ["human", "{note}"]
]);
const model = makeModel(['{"label":"vibration","evidence":"vibrates"}']);
const chain = prompt.pipe(model).pipe(new JsonOutputParser());
const note = "P-17 vibrates above 2500 rpm";
const result = await chain.invoke({note});
const schema = z.object({label:z.enum(["leak","vibration","other"]),
  evidence:z.string().min(1)}).strict();
schema.parse(result);
if (!note.includes(result.evidence)) throw Error("Unsupported evidence");
const queue = result.label === "other" ? "review" : "maintenance";
return {mode: MODEL_MODE, result, queue};

03 · Preparing Data and Checking Answers

§ Data for LLMs

Data for LLM ApplicationsDifferent data collections serve different purposes

Four collections, four different uses

Evaluation SetDefine expected behavior before changing the model or prompt

Every prompt version runs on the same frozen cases

Evaluation CasesCover routine requests, rare failures, and abstention

InputExpected behavior
Clear vibration reportLabel vibration; quote evidence
Conflicting measurementsFlag disagreement
Missing equipment identifierRequest clarification
Question without evidenceAbstain rather than invent
An evaluation set includes cases where answering is the failure

Synthetic DataGenerate candidates from a controlled seed and validate them

Generated notes stay candidates until checked

Synthetic Data ValidationCheck more than whether the generated example reads well

CheckMaintenance-note example
ValidityThe equipment type exists
Label consistencyEvidence supports the assigned label
CoverageInclude rare and ambiguous cases
SeparationKeep evaluation seeds out of training
Generated examples remain candidates until validated

Caveat: Synthetic CoverageGenerated variants may repeat the seed distribution

More variants of the seed add no new categories

Filtering and DeduplicationClean records and keep their provenance before splitting

Each stage removes records and keeps provenance

Exact DeduplicationHash normalized text and keep a reference to every source

import hashlib
def key(text):
    normalized = ' '.join(text.split())
    return hashlib.sha256(normalized.encode()).hexdigest()

# Group source records by key; retain provenance for the group.

Near-Duplicate DetectionSimilarity finds candidates that exact hashes miss

MethodWhat it comparesCaveat
Shingles / MinHashToken overlapMisses deep paraphrases
EmbeddingsSemantic similarityMay merge distinct facts
Source groupingDocument / event lineageNeeds metadata
Duplicate candidates need a task-specific merge rule

Dataset SplitKeep tuning examples separate from the final evaluation set

Paraphrases of one event stay in one split

Caveat: Near-Duplicate LeakageParaphrases can leak the same case across splits

Exact hashing misses a paraphrase of the same case

§ Evaluation and Release

Evaluation MetricsMeasure task correctness and system behavior separately

DimensionMeasure
Task successRubric pass rate
EvidenceSupported claims / evaluated claims
SchemaValid responses / responses
OperationsLatency, token cost, failure rate
One aggregate score cannot diagnose every failure

LLM-as-JudgeA judge applies a rubric to candidate outputs

Check the judge before trusting its scores

LLMOps TraceA trace connects the request to every intermediate step

The trace shows which step failed

Case study: Maintenance TriageA prompt change must survive the same labeled cases

VersionChangeComparison
p1Free-text labelsBaseline
p2Fixed enum + evidence fieldSchema failures
p3Explicit ambiguous-case policyWrong labels + abstentions
Changing the prompt changes the system under evaluation

Controlled LLM ReleasePromote the versioned application after regression checks

Freeze → Evaluate → Release → Monitor

Takeaway: Build and evaluate the whole LLM application

1Separate prompts, context, schemas, and control flow
2Curate evaluation data before optimizing the application
3Version the system and inspect failures in traces
